A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChunkFlow research. All 11 pages of each version, including algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen2.5 fine-tuning experiments comparing iteration times with Megatron-LM, plus memory measurements and ChunkSize/K sensitivity results in Section 6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports a practical estimate of grid-search overhead in Section 5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same chunk construction, state handling, and recomputation procedures, with unchanged state-aware 1F1B integration. The added GQA discussion explains memory behavior without introducing an architectural or procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use LMSysChat1M for motivating observations and the same constructed long-tail dataset for fine-tuning evaluation. No additional dataset, task, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Megatron-LM remains the experimental baseline, and standard 1F1B remains the scheduling comparison. The newly discussed LoRA is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: The Qwen2.5 model sizes, 32K/256K contexts, sequence filtering, batch sizes, iteration-time metric, and configurations in Tables 3–4 are unchanged. The new tuning-cost statement does not describe a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds a brief supplementary check of tuning cost, reporting grid-search overhead below 0.5% of total training time. The existing memory and ChunkSize/K sensitivity analyses in Section 6.3 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Reporting of average iteration times is unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports grid-search overhead below 0.5% of training time. Existing results match: Figure 8 retains all eight normalized iteration-time ratios, ranging from 2.13 to 4.53, and Tables 5–6 retain the same memory and timing values.

T1.justification: The bubble-ratio definition in Equation 1, scheduling assumptions, and mathematical-equivalence statement are retained. No formal definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: chunk construction, state-aware scheduling, memory control, and up to 4.53× speedup over Megatron-LM. Their claimed broader applicability is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly argues that GQA keeps stored key/value tensors and gradients from imposing significant memory overhead. Section 7 adds that parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA are orthogonal and compatible with ChunkFlow. The existing limitation concerning absent key/value offloading remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly discloses the grid-search cost as below 0.5% of total training time, although measurement details are not supplied. Hardware, hyperparameter configurations, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to GQA and LoRA and briefly positions ChunkFlow relative to parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Other reference changes principally update publication metadata or consolidate the duplicate Llama 3 citation, rather than change the research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the eight-section organization are retained. v3 adds short explanatory passages, an Impact Statement, acknowledgements, and conference metadata, alongside affiliation and bibliography edits.

P2.justification: Existing figures receive sharper rendering and several schematics are enlarged. Algorithm 2 and several figures are relocated, including Figure 8 moving from page 7 to page 8. The figure set, table structures, and plotted comparisons are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability through clearer figures and adds useful context about tuning cost, GQA memory behavior, and LoRA compatibility. These gains are limited: the method and principal experimental evidence are unchanged, and the new overhead estimate lacks measurement details.
